messages.subject: devtools:::find_pkg_topic - suggested correction to code when searching for a .Rd file
messages.subject_clean: devtools:::find_pkg_topic - suggested correction to code when searching for a .Rd file
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I think the line of code in find_pkg_topic the release version of devtools as at 3 August 2014 (devtools_1.5) which currently reads

man_rd <- file.path(pkg$path, "man", paste(topic, ".Rd"))

should really be

man_rd <- file.path(pkg$path, "man", paste(topic, ".Rd",sep=""))

to do what I think it is meant to be doing.

I'm sure there is a better way of suggesting this - but I'm working my way up a steep learning curve (steep for me anyway) trying to create and document my very first (baby) R package and this is the best I could figure out how to do.

Hope this helps

Geoff

PS devtools and roxygen2 are great. Really looking forward to the Advanced R book when it comes out!

Before I got your response I did do a little more experimenting.  I made 3 baby packages with various versions of a generic function (gen1) and attempts to add methods into the documentation using @rdname gen1.  I did manage to get documentation to appear when I added 'silly' methods for other generic functions that already existed (I played around adding silly methods for plot and @rdnaming the documentation into gen1.Rd). But when I cleaned everything up and restarted Rstudio, everything came out in the right order, and nothing I can do now seems to make it misbehave :-(

I suspect it is something to do with the order things accumulated in my RStudio 'environment' while I was experimenting with sequences of load_all(), document(), and dev_help('gen1') - roxygen and R appeared to have different opinions about what order things had occurred in.  But since I can't reproduce it, that's probably not much help.

Once again, many thanks for responding so promptly, and indeed for the complete devtools / roxygen2 suite of packages.

regards

Geoff

Hi

I've not worked my way through enough of the devtools code to properly understand the consequences of this idea, hence I am posing it as a question, not a suggestion.

I have come across a problem when I have an @include in a package hat has not yet been processed by using devtools::document(), and hence the automatically generated Collate: field in my DESCRIPTION file does not yet know about the @include tag.  If the default sort order of the filenames involved in the as yet unprocessed @include tag puts them in the wrong order, devtools::load_all() fails, somewhere around the load_code line in the following section of code

insert_imports_shims(pkg)
out$data <- load_data(pkg)
out$code <- load_code(pkg)
register_s3(pkg)

Because load_all() fails, the later steps in document() do not get run, and the Collate field in the DESCRPTION file does not get updated (unless by luck or trickery I comment out enough of the package code to get a Collate field generated that does what is needed, and then try again).

Example of my @include problem <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rdevtools/N3wy684ccnA>

>From my reading of documentation and perusal of devtools and roxygen2 code I suspect that a call to roxygen2:::update_collate would remedy this.  That would probably be mean adding a call something like

 with_envvar(r_env_vars(), roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg$path, roclets = 'collate', load_code = ns_env))

in the line before
out$code <- load-code(pkg)

 I haven't understood enough yet to be sure I've got the syntax of the roxygen2 call correct, nor that the arguments I have put in (which I have merely copied from later in the code of devtools::document) have actually been created or initialised at that stage of the load_all code, so it would need someone who knows more about how devtools works to vet / correct my suggestion.

Hoping this is useful

Regards

Geoff

PS I'm learning heaps by looking through the devtools code - many thanks to everyone who has put it together.

Hi again

After reading lots of code (VERY educational for me) and stepping through devtools::document in the debugger a few times, I think I'm getting closer to understanding what is going wrong in issue 261 https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/issues/261 .  I don't understand yet (9 Aug 2014) what should be done to fix it though .

My 'clue' is that I have observed that if you remove the method definition from the code, then run devtools::document() the .Rd file for the generic is created successfully.  If I then reinsert the code for the S4 method and run devtools::document() a second time, everything seems to work!

As suggested, the problem lies in (and downstream) of roxygen2::inherit_from.

inherit_from <- function (generic, pkg)
{
 if (pkg == "roxygen_devtest")
 return(generic)
 rd <- get_rd(generic, pkg)
 if (is.null(rd))
 return(NULL)
 if (!is.syntactic(generic)) {
 generic <- paste0("`", generic, "`")
 }
 paste0(pkg, "::", generic)
}

inherit_from calls get_rd(generic, package)

get_rd <- function (topic, package = NULL)
{
    help_call <- substitute(help(t, p), list(t = topic, p = package))
    top <- eval(help_call)
    if (length(top) == 0)
        return(NULL)
    internal_f("utils", ".getHelpFile")(top)
}

get_rd includes a line

top <- eval(help_call)

That is where the problem arises if the .Rd file for the generic does not already exist.  An error is raised, and eventually devtools::document() falls over.

If the help file for the generic is found, eval returns something which makes the rest of the code happy.

I'm not 100% sure that what it returns is what it should return - it seems to be some sort of structure which references the generic functions .Rd file.  I suspect (but haven't confirmed) that this will be the .Rd file from a previous run of devtools::document(), and hence may now be out of date if the user - aka me - has changed the documentation or definition of the generic function).

My guess is that this piece of code ought to be looking through the various bits of parsed code from the current run of devtools::document() that seem to be stored in the various environments devtools creates and manipulates.  But I'm still just learning about what an environment is and how devtools uses them, so I'm not able to go much further with this and actually propose a solution.

Hoping this helps someone who understands more than me to develop a solution for the issue.

regards

Geoff

messages.subject_clean: Issue relating to the order documentation appears in when using @include and @describeIn
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I have encountered something that doesn't make sense to me when using @include and @describeIn.  Possibly it is my expectations that are off track.  Anyway ...

The descriptions, the usage and the arguments appear in the generated documentation in the order of the (alpahabetically sorted) source file names, not the collated order from the DESCRIPTION file as generated (with some trickery) from the @include tags.  I think this occurs because roxygen2 initially parses the files in the alphabetic source file name order.

Here is a toy example to illustrate what I mean.

File ccode.r is
#' @title A generic function and its methods (from file ccode.r)
#' @description Description of gen (from cccode.r)
#' @details Details of gen (from ccode.r)
#' @param x The formal param - x - of gen (from ccode.r)
#' @param ... Any other parameters a specific method of gen may need (from ccode.r)
#'
setGeneric('gen',def=function(x, ...){standardGeneric('gen')})

File bcode.r is

#' @include ccode.r
#' @describeIn gen Description of meth1 for gen (from bcode.r)
#' @title Title of meth1 (from bcode.r)
#' @description Description of meth1 (numeric signature) (from bcode.r)
#' @details Details of meth1 (from bcode.r)
#' @param x The formal param of gen - x - for meth1 (from bcode.r)
#' @param bcode_param A formal param - bcode_param  - for meth1 (from bcode.r)

setMethod('gen', signature=signature('numeric'),
          def=function(x, bcode_param) {
            cat(x, bcode_param)
          }
)

File acode.r is
#' @include ccode.r bcode.r
#' @describeIn gen Description of meth2 for gen (from acode.r)
#' @title Title of meth2 (from acode.r)
#' @description Description of meth2 (character signature) (from acode.r)
#' @details Details of meth2 (from acode.r)
#' @param x The formal param of gen - x - for meth2 (from acode.r)
#' @param acode_param A formal param - acode_param - for meth2 (from acode.r)

setMethod('gen',signature=signature('character'),
          def=function(x, acode_param) {
            cat(x, acode_param)
          }
)

Although the files are named acode.r, bcode.r and ccode.r the collation order as specified via the @include tags is reversed namely ccode.r, bcode.r, acode.r

devtools::document() falls over if these are run in a totally clean environment (because it doesn't know about the correct collate order), but if I edit the collate order into the DESCRIPTION file by hand, as follows

Collate:
    'ccode.r'
    'bcode.r'
    'acode.r'

devtools::document() runs happily and produces documentation.  However the order of the entries is as I descibed earlier, in the alphabetical order of the source file names.  It looks like this

gen,character-method {paramsorderexample}  R Documentation
Title of meth2 (from acode.r)

Description

Description of meth2 (character signature) (from acode.r)

Description of meth1 (numeric signature) (from bcode.r)

Description of gen (from cccode.r)

Usage

## S4 method for signature 'character'
gen(x, acode_param)

## S4 method for signature 'numeric'
gen(x, bcode_param)

gen(x, ...)
Arguments

x
The formal param of gen - x - for meth2 (from acode.r)

acode_param
A formal param - acode_param - for meth2 (from acode.r)

x
The formal param of gen - x - for meth1 (from bcode.r)

bcode_param
A formal param - bcode_param - for meth1 (from bcode.r)

x
The formal param - x - of gen (from ccode.r)

...
Any other parameters a specific method of gen may need (from ccode.r)

Details

Details of meth2 (from acode.r)

Details of meth1 (from bcode.r)

Details of gen (from ccode.r)

Methods (by class)

character: Description of meth2 for gen (from acode.r)

numeric: Description of meth1 for gen (from bcode.r)

The .Rd file looks like this
%Generated by roxygen2 (4.0.1): do not edit by hand
\docType{methods}
\name{gen,character-method}
\alias{gen}
\alias{gen,character-method}
\alias{gen,numeric-method}
\title{Title of meth2 (from acode.r)}
\usage{
\S4method{gen}{character}(x, acode_param)

\S4method{gen}{numeric}(x, bcode_param)

gen(x, ...)
}
\arguments{
\item{x}{The formal param of gen - x - for meth2 (from acode.r)}

\item{acode_param}{A formal param - acode_param - for meth2 (from acode.r)}

\item{x}{The formal param of gen - x - for meth1 (from bcode.r)}

\item{bcode_param}{A formal param - bcode_param  - for meth1 (from bcode.r)}

\item{x}{The formal param - x - of gen (from ccode.r)}

\item{...}{Any other parameters a specific method of gen may need (from ccode.r)}
}
\description{
Description of meth2 (character signature) (from acode.r)

Description of meth1 (numeric signature) (from bcode.r)

Description of gen (from cccode.r)
}
\details{
Details of meth2 (from acode.r)

Details of meth1 (from bcode.r)

Details of gen (from ccode.r)
}
\section{Methods (by class)}{
\itemize{
\item \code{character}: Description of meth2 for gen (from acode.r)

\item \code{numeric}: Description of meth1 for gen (from bcode.r)
}}

I think it is happening because the load_code function in roxygen2::parse_package
parse_package <- function(base_path, load_code) {
  env <- load_code(base_path)
  parsed <- lapply(r_files(base_path), parse_file, env = env)
  blocks <- unlist(parsed, recursive = FALSE)

  list(env = env, blocks = blocks)
}

reads the code in source file name order, so the parsed code and the blocks created from it are in that order as well, and that flows through to when the .Rd documentation is generated.
Is this something I should raise here, or does it belong on the roxygen site?

Regards

Geoff

messages.subject: Bug fixes so as to use collation order better in devtools::load_all and roxygen2::parse_package
messages.subject_clean: Bug fixes so as to use collation order better in devtools::load_all and roxygen2::parse_package
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Apologies for duplications - I am still feeling my way about what belongs here, and what belongs on github.

Anyway ... I have trialled some 'proof of concept' tweaks to devtools::load_all and roxygen2::parse_package which I hope fixes some minor bugs in how inheritance and documenting inherited parameters are working (as at devtools 1.5.0.99 and roxygen2 4.0.1). They work on my toy example.  I have submitted them as pull requests.  My code is inelegant, and would not be used verbatim, but I hope it may be useful starting point for a someone with more experience to produce neater fixes.

Details follow below.

The devtools and roxygen2 code is fantastic - I have really enjoyed reading it and stepping through it in the debugger to see how it works on my toy example package.

Regards

Geoff Lee

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I have experienced a couple of related issues using the devtools / roxygen2 combination to develop and document a package.  Both issues relate to inheritance, and the file collation order for the package (which roxygen2 very nicely generates from the @include tags in the roxygen comments in my R code).

For details of the issues see :
  1) issue 261 , devtools::load_all not happy :
             https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/issues/261
             https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rdevtools/N3wy684ccnA
             https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rdevtools/2TMDbDcPNA8
             and
  2) issue related to order of (inherited) parameters in documentation from roxygen2
             https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rdevtools/KBd7X8UbqPg

These issues would be solved if :
  1) devtools::load_all updated the Collate field in the description file before attempting to load and evaluate the R code in the package
  and
  2) roxygen2::roxygenise read in and parsed the roxygen comment blocks from R files in the order of the Collate sequence instead of from R files in alphabetical filename sequence.

I have tried some 'proof of concept' tweaks to devtools::loadall and roxygen2::roxygenise to trial this, and they do solve my immediate problem.

My solutions are not as elegant and concise as the master devtools and roxygen code (which is awesome!), and have not been tested in other 'use cases', nor for efficiency, nor for other platforms (I am on Windows 7). But perhaps they will be useful small contribution as a rough starting point for other more experienced coders.

Regards

Geoff Lee

Hi,
I am replying to my own post. I still have this issue with devtools and Rcpp >= 0.11.0, but only under Linux. It works fine under Windows and apparently works fine under Mac. I have repeated the test on two other computers running Ubuntu and got the same issue so it doesn't seem to be related to my particular R installation.

I have a crude work around which involves dyn.load() and dyn.unload() to load / unload by hand the *.so file which gets placed in Rtmp after calling load_all(). The *.so file in Rtmp is the newly compiled file and works fine. This leads me to think that there is a problem with R 'reloading' the *.so after load_all() is called.

My compiler is gcc 4.8.2 which came with Ubuntu. I recently starting experimenting with clang 3.4. I compiled R with clang instead of gcc and my devtools and Rcpp problems went away. There seem to be no loading / unloading problems and using load_all() works as it used to with Rcpp 0.10. My conclusions: devtools and Rcpp >= 0.11.0 with gcc does not work properly under Linux, but with clang it does work properly.

I cannot pretend to understand what is going on or what the differences between clang and gcc are. Is this a known 'feature'? Has anyone else experienced these issues?

Yours

Finlay

This would recompile the source code, and update the RcppExports.R and .cpp files as necessary. The new exported function would then be immediately available to the current R session.

>
> # Then load devtools and use load_all()

>
> Does anyone else have experience of this, and a workaround?
>
> I am using Ubuntu 14.04 , R 3.1.0; x86_64, devtools 1.5
>
> Thanks
>
